OSM development/test environment setup automates the creation of an environment by preparing a base Debian cloud image and provisioning virtual machines (VMs) from it using cloud-init initialization system.
It is designed to provide a consistent, ready-to-use testing setup with minimal user effort.

* Create environment
#+begin_src bash
  ./run.bash -a setup|--action=setup -c <conf_file>|--config=<conf_file>
#+end_src

** User configuration file example
#+begin_export bash
  HOSTS_DIR="hosts"
  OSM_HOST_COUNT=3
  OSMCUSTOMER_COUNT=5
  VOSM_HOSTBR="osm_br0"
  OSM_SUBNET="192.168.5"
  HTTP_PORT=8088
  OSM_DOMAIN="osmm.fake.co.uk"
  MAIL_SMTP_HOST="smtp.gmail.com:587"
  MAIL_SMTP_USER="noreply@devtank.co.uk"
  MAIL_SMTP_PASSWORD="<change me>"
  MAIL_RECIPIENTS="<change me>"
#+end_export

* Remove environment
#+begin_src bash
  ./run.bash -a shutdown|--action=shutdown -d <hosts directory>|--hosts-dir=<hosts directory>
#+end_src

* Execute tests on running environment
#+begin_src bash
  ./run.bash -t|--run-tests -d <hosts directory>|--hosts-dir=<hosts directory>
#+end_src

* Preparation flow
** Stage 1
  - Fetch the latest amd64 [[https://cloud.debian.org/images/cloud/][Debian generic cloud image]]
  - Verify SHA512 checksum
  - Convert ext4 to btrfs file system

The process can be monitored via qemu_serial.log file or by accessing VM via SSH:
#+begin_src bash
  ssh -p 2222 root@localhost
#+end_src

** Stage 2
- Create network configuration
- Spawn VMs
  + VMs amount is configurable via OSM_HOST_COUNT in configuration file. Default is 3
  + VMs configuration is stored in the HOSTS_DIR directory. Default is "hosts"
- Install software by ansible orchestration system
